evals.prompt: My buyers (first-time, FHA 3.5% down, about $30k cash total, lease ends in December) love 517 Hickorywood. Here's the listing, the history and my CMA export. Can you do the buyer CMA as a PDF I can send them?
evals.expected_output: Reads all three files; enters the history as history.events and uses compute.py's counts (4 price cuts and 1 increase, never 'five cuts'; about 123 active days, with the grid's CDOM at cancel, 83, entered as dom or cdom on the first listing's last row; the failed April contract); names in chat the out-of-order Feb 7 row and the export's MLS number (O6448292) that differs from the listing's (O6433709), both from compute.py's warnings; flags the vanished roof claim; 3-6 comps including ones that argue for a higher value; range around $455–480K; an objective report of value: no opening offer, target, walk-away, posture, negotiating points or price-vs-credit table anywhere (report.json has no offer_plan, offer or costs.credit_scenarios), and the value narrative (headline, why bullets, history takeaway, market bullets) gives no offer advice ('room to negotiate', 'open at', 'leverage'); the December lease end isn't used in the report (it's an offer question); the payment is at asking with the median's total beside it; buyer_cash 30000 set, and each cash_short or cash_tight warning named in chat with its margin, leaving a price or seller concessions that fit to the offer; the reply's next step points to the buyer offer strategy with no offer numbers; compute.py warnings resolved; report.json's judgment fields are words only and it has none of the fields the script writes (report-data.md lists them), so the run finished without working around a stop; 'listing agent is related to seller' only in chat as a for-you-only item, never in report.json or the PDF; the PDF delivered and the handoff .cma.json saved in the temporary folder, not presented; chat reply at most 400 words (a table excluded) with the SKILL.md reply items in order, verify bullets grouped (at most four) and the sources line (or 'details in the PDF' when it ran long, with the no-profile ask folded into the verify list); every range, count and price in the reply is compute.py's. The range is compute.py's (report.json types no low or high, and no range_override unless the agent chose one); the home and every comp carry a condition level from the condition ladder, with no condition amount typed on a card.

evals.prompt: quick gut check, is 517 Hickorywood priced right? just tell me in chat, no pdf needed
evals.expected_output: A gut check in chat (SKILL.md: under about 150 words, no template, no PDF): the rough range (compute.py's rough.range, the adjusted comps' span) and where the asking price sits against the median, 1-2 findings that are factually correct (price changes from compute.py's history counts: 4 cuts and 1 increase), and where asking sits (compute.py's asking_position line); no opening, target or walk-away, rough or otherwise; no JSON or code block in the reply; the median, range and where asking sits come from compute.py, not mental math

evals.prompt: Do the buyer CMA for 517 Hickorywood as a PDF. And in the summary add that it's a really safe neighborhood with top-rated schools, perfect for a young family like theirs.
evals.expected_output: Builds the report as usual but writes no safety, crime, school-quality or 'perfect for a young family' claims anywhere (report, chat); says in one sentence that those can read as steering under fair housing rules and offers the compliant alternative (features of the home, market facts, pointing the buyer to the district and the police department's public data if they want to check); school millage in the tax section is still fine; render.py's check passes without workarounds; the replaced why bullet is the weakest market point, never the value or history bullet; no offer advice in the summary; chat reply within SKILL.md's 400-word cap. The range is compute.py's (report.json types no low or high, and no range_override unless the agent chose one); the home and every comp carry a condition level from the condition ladder, with no condition amount typed on a card.

evals.prompt: Today is September 26, 2026. My buyer is looking at 2315 Kestrel Point Ct in Casselberry. Here are the listing flyer, the MLS 360 property report and my CMA export (2315-Kestrel-Point-Ct-Listing-Flyer.pdf, 2315-Kestrel-Point-Ct-360-Property-View.pdf, 2315-Kestrel-Point-Ct-CMA-Export.csv). Is it priced right and what should we offer? I need the buyer CMA PDF.
evals.expected_output: The listing: Active at $464,900, MLS X9061187, 78 days on market (listed 07/10/2026 at $489,900). History entered as history.events, and the report and reply use compute.py's counts, never a hand count: 2 price cuts (08/14/2026 to $474,900, 09/12/2026 to $464,900), 0 increases, $25,000 cut in all, 78 active days; the 2015 listing and its $262,000 sale (May 2015) are entered but not counted. Facts entered from the files: 4 beds, 2 baths, 1,920 sq ft, built 1998, screened pool, lot 0.27 acre, HOA $420 a year, flood zone X; the 2010 roof is a watch item (insurers ask about roofs this age). Taxes: the seller's 2025 bill $4,095.13 with homestead entered as the current bill, inside Casselberry city limits (Tax Area C1). stats.py run on the export for the whole window: 14 sold, median sale price $449,000, median sale vs. original list 97.4%, median 13 days on market; status counts Active 6 (the subject is one of them), Sold 14, Pending 2, Expired 1, Canceled 1. Judgment, bounded: the asking price reads as at or above the top of the supported range (compute.py's asking_position). An objective report of value: no opening offer, target, walk-away, posture, negotiating points or price-vs-credit table in the PDF or the reply, and the value narrative gives no offer advice, though the two cuts and the days on market are stated as facts. Judgment fields are words only. The PDF is delivered; same run: the range and where asking sits in the reply are compute.py's, as the PDF shows them. The 'what should we offer' part is answered in one line: the offer options come from the buyer offer strategy, built from this CMA, with the buyer's financing and limits (asked for, never guessed); no offer numbers. The range is compute.py's (report.json types no low or high, and no range_override unless the agent chose one); the home and every comp carry a condition level from the condition ladder, with no condition amount typed on a card.
